_doc: Anti-drift compass for the LOGBOOK DEEPWALK EXPANSION arc (Ian 2026-07-28: 'proceed to logbook roadmap next'). Companion to LOGBOOK_DEEPWALK_EXPANSION_ROADMAP.md. tools/logbook_deepwalk_scoreboard.py reads this and emits a MEASURED % per phase and per LG class. EXPANSION means growing BOTH denominators: journeys x personas x states (board 1) and new LG dimension classes (board 2). A cell moves only on cited live evidence.
_phases_def: ground - map the surfaces, handlers, tables and caches the journey touches
walk - live-MCP journey walk carrying the full lens; requires >=2 personas AND >=2 states
observe - record friction with evidence (a clean walk is a real result, record it as such)
harvest - Engine B, at spoke 5 ONLY, for a friction the walk actually surfaced
resolve - fix, then LOCK with a gate; a fix without a gate is not done
_coverage_rule: A journey's W phase is 'done' only when walked in >=2 personas AND >=2 states. One-persona/one-state is the shallowness this arc exists to kill.

LB07.notes: WALKED LIVE 2026-07-28. Happy path clean end-to-end (offline insert -> queue -> reload keeps it queued -> reconnect -> DB row with correct auth_uid/hive_id; offline edit -> sync -> applied, updated_at touched by trg_logbook_touch_updated_at so the sync payload's missing updated_at is NOT a defect). DEFECT FOUND (S-error): a queued update matching 0 rows returns {error:null,status:204}, so `if (!error)` dropped the queued item and toasted '1 offline change synced.' while writing nowhere - proven by deleting the row server-side mid-offline, then confirming DB row absent + queue drained + success toast. 0 rows is the NORMAL RLS outcome (logbook UPDATE is owner-scoped on auth_uid, SELECT is hive-scoped). Same shape in the SHARED offline-queue.js drain() reaching 6 more surfaces. FIXED in both (read rows back, treat empty as unconfirmed, keep the worker's text, dead-letter, say so out loud); badge + feed-merge reconciled to the new _stalled state. LB09.notes: Walked 2026-07-28 while driving LB7; saveEditFromForm exercised online AND offline as P-worker. FOUND: the page collapsed three different 0-row causes into one message ('Entry was modified by someone else, reload...'), which is right for a concurrent edit and WRONG for the other two - and in the ownership case no reload can ever help. Worse, 72 of Pablo's 571 entries had auth_uid IS NULL while UPDATE/DELETE require auth_uid = auth.uid(), so the UI offered Edit and Delete on rows the database would ALWAYS refuse (verified: an update of one applied nothing, no error). RESOLVED BOTH WAYS: (a) DATA - migration 20260728000000_logbook_auth_uid_backfill.sql binds auth_uid from the unambiguous worker_name->auth_uid mapping in hive_members (skips any name resolving to 2+ accounts rather than guessing, since attribution IS the DOLE/ISO trail); applied locally, 72 rows repaired, re-run is a no-op, and the previously-uneditable row now updates (1 row affected, live-verified). (b) CODE - one explainZeroRowWrite() resolver used by BOTH the online save and the offline drain, so the two paths cannot tell the worker different stories; all 3 reachable branches verified live (deleted / someone else's / concurrent-edit). HARVEST: NN/g error-message guidelines (state the cause + a real remedy), the same standard MK11 cites. GATE: the offline half is locked by validate_offline_queue_confirm.py. W stays PARTIAL at one persona. THIRD FIX (the small one that turned out not to be small): openEditModal is async and set _editingId only at the END, after an entry re-fetch and an await on renderReadingsFields(), while the save button stayed LIVE - so a fast tap ran saveEditFromForm() with _editingId still null, which offline enqueues under a null IndexedDB keyPath, THROWS, and strands the form with a permanently disabled button. Fixed at the source (hold the button with a 'Loading...' label for the whole populate, release it where _editingId is set, and hand it back on the not-found path) plus a defence-in-depth guard in saveEditFromForm. Both verified live: during the await the button is disabled/'Loading...' with _editingId null, after it is enabled/'Update Entry' with the id set; the guard toasts 'That entry is still loading' and recovers the button instead of stranding it.

LB10.notes: WALKED LIVE 2026-07-28 as Pablo against David Velasco's and Ricardo Morales's entries in the same hive. THE DATA BOUNDARY IS REAL, not cosmetic - the strong probe: a direct client UPDATE and a direct DELETE on a teammate's row with the client's own worker_name filter REMOVED, so nothing but RLS stood in the way; both affected 0 rows and the row was verified untouched afterwards. So this is NOT a hole. THE GLASS WAS DISHONEST though: the entry-detail modal rendered 'Edit Entry' and 'Delete' identically on a teammate's entry as on your own, a dead affordance walking the worker into a guaranteed refusal (and before today's LB9 fix, into a message blaming a concurrent editor who did not exist). Only the person who wrote an entry can edit or delete it.' Verified live both ways: teammate's entry = 0 buttons + the note, own entry = Edit + Delete, and all 200 of my own entries still writable (no regression). Used the canonical ic-secure icon after checking that the ic-lock I first reached for does not exist in wh-icons.css. LB17.notes: WALKED LIVE 2026-07-28 as Christine Dizon (worker in Manila, supervisor in Lucena). DEFECT FOUND: the server read is hive-filtered but the pending-queue MERGE was not, so after capturing offline in Manila and switching to Lucena the Manila entry rendered as a real card ('Pending sync') inside the Lucena feed - one tenant's work shown in another tenant's context. What is CORRECT and must stay: the queued row keeps its CAPTURE-time hive_id and syncs into THAT hive, not the current one (verified in the DB), which is why filtering is the right fix and re-homing would be wrong. FIXED (merge scoped to the active hive, reading hive_id from both the insert shape and the update shape - a first cut missed queued EDITS entirely because they carry hive_id inside `updates`). Re-verified all four ways: hidden in Lucena, still queued, visible again in Manila, lands in Manila on sync. GATED in validate_offline_queue_confirm.py (audit_queue_hive_scope); teeth proven on real pre-fix code. LG1.name: Mutation-contract parity
LG1.enumeration_2026_07_28: SWEEP DONE - every client mutation of the logbook table, platform-wide: logbook.html L1764 offline-drain update (FIXED: .select + 0-row confirm), L1769 offline-drain insert, L1994 addEntry insert (carries auth_uid), L3877 saveEdit fallback update, saveEditFromForm (FIXED: .select + 0-row guard, honest explainer); pm-scheduler.html L2062 the PM mirror insert; integrations.html L1244 CMMS batch insert and L2016+L2021 status updates. THREE FINDINGS NOT YET FIXED: (1) saveEdit() at L3824 is DEAD CODE - defined but called from NOWHERE in the live page (the only saveEdit('...') invocation is in logbook.backup.html, which this arc ignores by scope, plus one static test regex that also accepts saveEditFromForm). So the 'two edit paths' the PDDA arc flagged is really ONE live path plus a dead one. It matters because the dead path carries the 0-row-blind shape AND calls writeAuditLog() unconditionally afterwards, so were it ever wired up it would record a DOLE/ISO amendment for an edit the database refused. Right disposition for defect-carrying dead code is DELETE, not fix - fixing it would imply it is live. (2) Its OC-guard branch may be dead too: it needs existing.updated_at, and the loadEntries mapper does not appear to carry updated_at into the cache, which is the known dead-OC-guard shape. Worth confirming before deleting, because it decides whether saveEditFromForm needs the guard instead. (3) integrations.html resolveConflict() - FIXED AND LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-28, and it was the worst instance because the whole point of that console is reconciliation. Both branches wrote with NO check; the try/catch caught nothing because supabase-js RETURNS { error } rather than throwing, and a 0-row update is not even an error. loadConflicts() deliberately excludes the CMMS-sync accounts, so every row it offers belongs to a REAL worker while logbook UPDATE is owner-scoped - a supervisor resolving a teammate's conflict changed nothing, was told 'Resolved: logbook updated to match SAP', and left the two systems diverged with the same conflict still listed. SECOND BUG in the same function: the 'Keep WorkHive' branch updated `logbook` with the status it already had - a no-op contradicting both its own comment and its toast ('SAP will receive the update on next push'); keeping WorkHive means writing OUR status onto the EXTERNAL record. Both fixed and walked live against a seeded conflict (external_sync was EMPTY platform-wide, so the fixture had to be built to make the flow walkable at all): 'Keep WorkHive' now moves external_sync Closed->Open and leaves the logbook untouched, and 'Use SAP' on David Velasco's entry leaves it Closed and says 'A logbook entry can only be changed by the worker who wrote it' instead of claiming success. Fixture removed afterwards (external_sync back to 0 rows).
LG1.notes: Harvest = PDDA 2026-07-12: INSERT sets auth_uid, BOTH update paths omit it. DEFINED 2026-07-28 by the LB9 walk, and the rule is sharper than the original framing: an UPDATE omitting auth_uid is NOT itself the bug (the row keeps the auth_uid bound at insert, and the trg_bind_submitter_logbook trigger owns that). The real parity rule is that every mutating path must agree on how it CONFIRMS and EXPLAINS a write - which they did not: the online path checked rows and the offline drain did not, and each had its own story for the same failure. FIX PARTIAL: the confirmation and the explanation are now single-sourced (explainZeroRowWrite + the .select confirmation in both paths), and the auth_uid data gap that made the mismatch user-visible is backfilled. NOT DONE: the full enumeration of every logbook mutation site (saveEdit modal vs saveEditFromForm vs deleteEntry vs the PM mirror vs voice/photo capture) against one contract, and no detector or gate yet holds that parity - that is the class's next stage.

LG3.name: Offline-queue reconciliation — a queued write is a CACHE, and 0 rows is not 'synced'
LG3.notes: EARNED BY THE LB7 WALK 2026-07-28 (born from observed friction, per the arc's rule). RULE: a drain that removes a queued item must confirm the write actually affected a row - PostgREST returns error:null/204 for a 0-row update or delete, so branching on `error` alone destroys the worker's only copy and reports success. HARVEST: web.dev offline-UX guidelines ('never silent-fail, never false-success'; 'on reconnect tell the user what synced + surface any conflict needing their resolution, do not silently overwrite or drop'). SWEEP: all 3 drain sites platform-wide (offline-queue.js whCreateQueue+drain serving 6 surfaces, logbook.html syncOfflineQueue). FIX: read the rows back; empty = UNCONFIRMED not failed (on inventory_items a hive_id-NULL row is writable but not readable, so empty can also mean 'applied, not visible'); keep the item, dead-letter it, tell the user. GATE: tools/validate_offline_queue_confirm.py, registered, teeth proven by reverting to HEAD.

LG5.name: Transition tenant-integrity — data in flight carries CAPTURE-time identity
LG5.notes: EARNED BY THE LB17 WALK 2026-07-28. RULE: a queue/draft/filter holds the hive it was CAPTURED in; a hive switch must neither re-home it (data) nor display it outside that hive (glass). The hive arc locked the ROLE marker; this is the DATA-in-flight analog. Evidence: a Manila entry captured offline rendered as a live card in the Lucena feed after a switch, because the pending-queue merge was unfiltered while the server read was hive-scoped. FIX + GATE as recorded on LB17. SWEEP COMPLETE, and it came back CLEAN - a real result, recorded as such: every other queue surface (community, dayplanner, inventory, pm-scheduler, skillmatrix, asset-hub FMEA) only ENQUEUES; none reads the queue back to render a list, so none can leak a queued row across hives. logbook.html is the only page that merges pending items into its feed, which is why it was the only page with this defect - the same shape as the hive arc's finding that hive.html was the only page mutating role without a reload. Their payloads also carry capture-time hive_id, so the drain cannot re-home them either.

LG9.name: Role boundary on glass vs data
LG9.notes: EARNED BY THE LB10 WALK 2026-07-28. RULE: every write affordance must be gated on the SAME predicate the server enforces - RLS stays the enforcement, the glass must not offer what the database will always refuse. Evidence: Edit and Delete rendered on teammates' entries whose owner-scoped RLS refuses every write (proven with the client filter removed: 0 rows, row untouched). This is HK1 from the hive arc re-applied to WRITE affordances rather than to a role marker, and the answer came out the opposite way: hive.html's boundary was real AND its chrome was wrong; here the boundary is real and the chrome was wrong in a quieter way - it offered an action instead of leaking data. SWEEP PARTIAL: only the entry-detail modal is audited. The feed cards, the asset manager on this same page (asset_nodes upsert/update/delete) and the parts/inventory actions have not been checked for the same offer-what-RLS-refuses shape.

LG8.name: Mirror integrity, both directions
LG8.notes: OPENED ON MEASURED EVIDENCE and RESOLVED 2026-07-28. fault_knowledge.logbook_id had NO foreign key at all - the table's only FK was hive_id - so deleting an entry left its knowledge row behind, still embedded and still retrievable, citing an entry that no longer exists. 21 dangling rows measured against the PDDA arc's 529/529-valid reading of 2026-07-12. CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER CLAIM: I first reported 'none from this session', which was WRONG - that check looked only at the 10 most recent orphans and missed mine. One of the 21 WAS the entry I deleted during the LB7 walk, and its mirror had preserved the full content (WLD-001 / 'Output current unstable, weld quality poor' / 'Mechanical Damage' / 'Replaced 4 carbon brushes, cleaned commutator' / 'Carbon brushes 80% worn'). FIX: migration 20260728000001 adds the FK with ON DELETE CASCADE, because the knowledge row is DERIVED from the entry, so a retracted entry must not leave a citable ghost in the RAG. Walked BOTH lineage directions live per the anti-seesaw discipline: deleting an entry now cascades its knowledge row (1 -> 0, in a rolled-back transaction) and inserting knowledge for a nonexistent entry is REFUSED with a clear FK error. NOT VALID is deliberate: it enforces everything going forward without retroactively judging pre-existing rows. Cleanup deleted the 20 dangling rows that are unambiguously probe residue from earlier sessions (K2-PROBE-* and two D2 helper/refix probes) and deliberately did NOT touch the one real orphan, which is a data decision for Ian, not something a migration should make quietly. GATE: extended tools/validate_logbook_asset_linkage.py (same lineage domain, live-tier, skips cleanly without docker); teeth proven by DROPPING the constraint (exit 1) and restoring it (pass). SWEEP PARTIAL: the sibling mirrors - pm_knowledge.pm_completion_id, skill_knowledge, project_links - have not been checked for the same missing-FK shape.
